subject: unmarked - Gdistsamp : Problems obtaining model fit

messages.author: 1b748f4efa4a618b
messages.subject: unmarked - Gdistsamp : Problems obtaining model fit
parts:
Hello,

I am only writing this e-mail after recurring to all options I could think of on my code.

Briefly, the problem is:

I have my data correctly put together in unmarked framework, and tried to model with the Distsamp function (for Poisson distribution on abundance). After obtaining the best model, I procceed to test with GoF methods described in the Kery and Royle book (Thank you very much for that!) and the models show a  poor fit. However, this does not surprise me since overdispersion is to be expected, from previous data.

I then proceed to change my frame to work with Gdistsamp and test with Negative Binomial.
I even rerun most of the models to make sure the best models keep consistent, but when I go to test the best models selected by AIC with the function fitstats using the parboot  function I end up getting the same error that I got several times when I tried to optimize my models throughout all previous attempts. It's producing a "2 to 3 node errors: vmin value not finite. ".
I got this sometimes during  the model development part, but providing starting values that made sense I could then obtain my models. However, I don't know how to do this, or if it even makes sense to do so with parboot. I tried to run the sims in parallel and with seeds to get multiple tries in and also modified the function tested (fitstats) to perform only 1, or combinations of 2 of the 3 tests it performs, thinking that may be the estimates with the chi-squared formula might be what was leading to this. But it still didn't work.

If anyone has run into something similar or can help me explore or circunvent this problem I would be extremely grateful. I can also provide more information on my data and errors if needed.

Thank you very much in advance!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] unmarked - Gdistsamp : Problems obtaining model fit
parts:
Dear Joao,

that's a problem with the optimisation algorithm for the model fitting, not a problem with the fit statistics.

When you parboot, does the "vmin value not finite" error happen with every single bootstrap iteration ? I think I had this same problem sometime, but it did not occur with every bootstrap iteration and so I accumulated a sample of about 100 'by hand', by copy-pasting the output values of t.star or what it's called into another file, and then doing the p-value calcs myself.

Best regards  --  Marc
